messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH severity: GPU pool saturation detected in us-east-1. autoscaler failing to provision new hotpools. 90th pct latency spike, elevated 429s across models. paging oncall (Sophie Li)
Sophie Li: seeing consistent 429s for hotspot customers — traces show queue depth growing on the hotpath queue for model 'redwood-13b-opt'
Arjun Patel: adding context — autoscaler logs show repeated `resource_limit` on pool creation, followed by `tokenbucket: rate limit exceeded` errors when trying to hand off queued requests. looks like a combined quota + tokenbucket misconfiguration during surge
Maria Gomez: confirmed. heatmap: GPU pool usage 100% for 18m, queued requests ~14k, 429s correlate with tokenbucket rejects at the tier layer. autoscaler attempted 3 scale cycles and hit pool max size (pool cap set by capacity contract)
Jake Chen: customer impact — 3 paying customers showing degraded latency and elevated error rates. CS pinged them already. Need immediate mitigation: reduce tokenbucket strictness, bump refill/burst, and open emergency capacity if possible
Priya Singh: I'm on it. exploring two quick mitigations: 1) relax token bucket refill rate for the affected tier, 2) temporarily route new requests to best-effort lower-tier GPU pool to relieve hotpath. preference is 1) first — quicker config change.
Sophie Li: agree. what changed recently? any rollout that modified tier policies?
Arjun Patel: there was a ratepolicy rollout 70m ago that tightened burst windows for the mid-tier to protect infra costs — it looks like it reduced the `token_window` from 60s to 10s and decreased burst allowance. under steady state fine, but under a surge it starves hotpath and prevents autoscaler from getting enough successful handoffs to trigger backfill
Priya Singh: applying temporary tokenbucket tweak now — increasing `refill_rate` + `burst` for `prod-mid` tier. command: 

```
# api call to admin service
POST /admin/tokenbucket/tune
{
  "tier": "prod-mid",
  "refill_rate": "+200",
  "burst": "+150"
}
```

Priya Singh: pushed change. deploy-bot: config apply in progress
deploy-bot: config-update:tokenbucket: succeeded for prod-mid (change-id: cb-9923). rollback window 10m
Maria Gomez: autoscaler logs after tweak: more successful handoffs, but still hitting pool capacity. need to either increase pool cap (requires approvals) or temporarily allow cross-tier routing
Jake Chen: can we enable cross-tier best-effort routing? fallback policy exists but was disabled during the ratepolicy rollout.
Arjun Patel: yes, we can: set routing policy `allow_cross_tier_fallback=true` for the affected route. I'll flip it but will limit to non-critical customers so we don't violate SLAs unintentionally
Priya Singh: flipping flag now -> `PATCH /admin/routing/allow_cross_tier_fallback?route=hotpath&limit=non_critical`
deploy-bot: routing-flag:update: success (id: rf-4412)
Priya Singh: traffic starting to shift off hotpool -> queue depth down from 14k to 5.2k in ~6m
Sophie Li: 429 rate dropping, customers reporting fewer errors. continuing to monitor. still measuring increased token spend; finance/observability will want numbers for postmortem
Maria Gomez: note — autoscaler didn't honor scale intent earlier because of a throttling loop: tokenbucket rejects prevented successful handoffs, which suppressed the metric that triggers scale-up. once tokenbucket relaxed and cross-tier routing enabled, we saw successful handoffs and autoscaler resumed backfill attempts
Arjun Patel: root cause hypothesis: recent ratepolicy rollout tightened token_window and burst for mid tier; under surge this created a feedback loop that prevented autoscaler progress and saturated already-constrained GPU pool. secondary factor: pool cap induced by reserved capacity contract blocked immediate scale.
Jake Chen: mitigation summary posted to ops channel and CS updated customers. next immediate steps: 1) keep tokenbucket relaxed for 30m, 2) keep fallback routing on for non-critical classes, 3) request emergency capacity from capacity team if pool stays >95% after 30m
Priya Singh: reverted tight rollout partial change: opened rollback MR to restore previous `token_window=60s` for prod-mid. MR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/merge_requests/4321
Sophie Li: oncall handoff in 30m -> handing to oncall-switch. leaving notes: watch queue depth, 429 rate, tokenbucket reject counter `tb_rejects.prod-mid`, and autoscaler backfill success metric `autoscaler.backfill.success`
oncall-switch: taking over. acknowledged. will run the post-incident checklist and coordinate with capacity team.
Sophie Li: final quick customer impact note for postmortem: ~45m duration of elevated errors, top-tier customers experienced ~12% increased 95p latency and intermittent 429s. mitigation reduced impact within ~12m after tokenbucket tweak + routing flag. include timeline & config diffs in postmortem.
Arjun Patel: adding operational recommendations for the postmortem: 1) prevent token_window reductions during active rollouts without a canary that simulates surge, 2) add an autoscaler health metric that ignores tokenbucket rejects when computing scale intent, 3) create a runbook step to temporarily bypass tokenbucket for autoscaler-originated handoffs
Priya Singh: logging config diffs and saving commands used. I'll collect the commands and apply to the incident runbook doc
Sophie Li: thanks team. marking incident as 'mitigated' — will update status once capacity team responds.
incident-bot: Incident 3012345678 status: mitigated -> monitoring. followups: postmortem assigned to Arjun + Priya.
